chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

There is many a person who fasts whose fast is nothing but just hunger and thirst, and many an offerer of prayers whose prayer is no better than wakefulness and hardship. The sleep as well as the eating and drinking of the intelligent (God-knowing) person is far better.

key_terms.إِفْطَارُهُمْ: their breaking of the fast / eating and drinking

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between physical fasting and spiritual fasting in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this famous saying from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) critiques the phenomenon of *ghurur* (spiritual delusion) where physical acts of worship, such as fasting and night prayer, become hollow rituals devoid of *khushu* (humility and presence of heart). He contrasts the 'empty' worshipper, who gains only the physical sensations of hunger and fatigue, with the *akyaas* (discerning ones) whose rituals are infused with spiritual insight, thereby elevating their rest and sustenance above the mere mechanical observance of the negligent.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 145. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:

There is many a person who fasts whose fast is nothing but just hunger and thirst, and many an offerer of prayers whose prayer is no better than wakefulness and hardship. The sleep as well as the eating and drinking of the intelligent (God-knowing) person is far better.
